auth.quote: There are two ways to get a Bearer token — through API tokens in your settings or through an OAuth implementation
OAuth is required for public integrations available to all Front customers unless you obtain an exception from us.

access.quote: If you don't already have an account, you'll want to sign up for a free development account.
By default, apps are private to the Front instance they are created in.
If you want to make an app available for all Front customers to use, you must publish your app.
We are currently an open integration platform and approve the vast majority of integrations submitted to us.
By default, Front's API rate limit starts at 50 requests per minute and varies depending on your plan.

api.quote: Access resources allows you to manage Core API resources such as conversations, contacts, inboxes, etc.
List the views accessible to the authenticated token.

mcp.quote: Front's MCP server (mcp.frontapp.com/mcp) lets AI agents act on Front conversation data using a single OAuth-authenticated endpoint.
Front does not support Dynamic Client Registration.

buildability.quote: To publish your app, notify our team as described in the Partnering with Front topic.
Smaller teams may also be subject to a security or legal review.

uncertain.access: Free development account gives working API tokens and a private OAuth app immediately (self-serve for single-instance use). Multi-customer OAuth requires publishing via Front's 'Partnering with Front' process (submission + approval, described as approving the vast majority). Labelled approval_required; a grader could read the 'partnership program' wording as partner_gated.
uncertain.mcp: Official vendor-hosted endpoint confirmed; it requires a confidential OAuth client (client ID + secret) created in Front developer settings, no DCR.

notes: Front docs llms.txt index lists ~350 /reference/ entries (~329 excluding plugin SDK helpers), so Core API is broad. Front also runs a separate Admin MCP server. MCP OAuth is user-scoped so any teammate can authorize, whereas regular OAuth app authorization requires an admin. Pricing page lists the API rate-limit add-on as 'Available on all plans'; no free production plan exists, only the free developer account.
